reason: Before the change, the formatter matched unsupported Y tokens and fell through to the timezone-offset fallback, so the lone Y and YYY outputs would not be the required literals.
The revised format token handling excludes unsupported single and triple Y tokens from the timezone fallback, preserving Y literally and formatting YYY as YY followed by Y.
The pull request only centralizes the existing percent-decoding check; route parameters were already decoded before and remain decoded after the refactor.
The new utility performs the same percent-decoding operation previously used inline for route parameters, so the decoded route value is preserved.
Before the fix, reschedule updates Redis but leaves the same SortedEntry object’s @score unchanged, so score and at remain stale.
The change assigns the new timestamp to @score after rescheduling, so both score and at on the existing handle reflect the requested time.
The patch changes Range-header parsing only; Content-Type parsing with a charset parameter is unrelated and should retain its existing behavior.
The Range whitespace fix does not touch Content-Type parsing, so this ordinary charset parsing behavior is unchanged.
The pull request only changes repository download error messages, not archive creation or ZIP timestamp handling; the described archive behavior is expected to remain available.
Neither the repeated archive operation nor extracted file timestamps is affected by the logging-only changes in ComposerRepository.
CredentialCache path comparison is unrelated to System.Text.Json, and standard asynchronous deserialization supports nullable reference properties in a list.
The revision changes only CredentialCache URI-prefix matching, so synchronous and asynchronous JSON deserialization should continue to produce equivalent results.
The cursor fix concerns FETCH FIRST on an empty held cursor, not INET containment or ANY-subquery parsing; the stated INET query should retain its existing support.
The change is isolated to cursor iteration and does not affect INET operators or ANY over an INET array, so the described query remains successful.
Before the fix, NO_PROXY entries were always treated as wildcard domains, so the raw IPv6 value ::1 could produce an invalid URL pattern and client construction could fail.
The fix recognizes IPv6 NO_PROXY values and creates the bracketed [::1] pattern, avoiding the prior parsing failure.
Before this pull request, passing DOTALL to Series.str.match was among the non-IGNORECASE flag combinations that raised instead of matching the newline.
The revised match logic preserves and applies DOTALL for both a string pattern and a compiled pattern, producing the requested True/False results.
The described middle-of-chain group is the recursive-parent case addressed by the pull request, so the base revision can lose result children during reconstruction.
The fix updates the previous task and result after processing the group, preserving the result-parent chain across the subsequent group and final task.
The reported bug is specifically when the value terminator is the first argument; with values already consumed before --, this trailing handoff should already parse correctly.
The patch preserves the first-positional terminator behavior and does not break the separate case where -- follows existing values and hands --check to the later positional.
A late OSC11 response used the old option-setting call, which triggers OptionSet after startup, and the background update also triggers the ColorScheme event.
The head revision deliberately uses noautocmd when applying the OSC11 background value, suppressing the required OptionSet event even though the background and ColorScheme update occur.
The pull request only changes compile-time handling of @derive dependencies and does not alter casting or required-field validation, so the omitted field remains invalid.
Reordering the @derive attribute read has no runtime effect on Ecto changesets; validate_required still reports the omitted mandatory field as blank.
